open_points.subject: INV-001, INV-017 and PLAT-REG-003 witness binding
open_points.text: “Witnesses, the focused Factory verification checks that assert it: INV-001, INV-017, PLAT-REG-003 [witness: verification:authorization_guard_client_portal].”
open_points.question: Which bound check will fully demonstrate first-failure ordering, uniqueness of active staff assignments, and refusal of a Registry validation answer whose UUID differs from the requested UUID?
options: Extend the named check to assert every omitted case
Bind additional checks that assert the omitted cases
Narrow the invariants to what the named check establishes
open_points.default_guess: Extend the named check with the omitted cases.

open_points.subject: INV-004 witness binding
open_points.text: “Witnesses, the focused Factory verification checks that assert it: INV-004 [witness: verification:staff_identity_uow_client_portal].”
open_points.question: What check demonstrates that every authentication failure is externally indistinguishable and cannot expose project data, rather than only comparing selected rejection types?
options: Extend the named check across all observable failure information and project-data outputs
Bind another comprehensive concealment check
Narrow INV-004
open_points.default_guess: Extend the named check across all authentication failure classes and observable outputs.

open_points.subject: PLAT-REG-006 witness bindings
open_points.text: “Witnesses, the focused Factory verification checks that assert it: PLAT-REG-006 [witness: verification:authorization_guard_client_portal]; PLAT-REG-006 [witness: verification:derived_views_uow_client_portal].”
open_points.question: Which check proves both that no Registry snapshot is stored or treated as current truth and that archived live context remains readable but cannot authorize mutation?
options: Extend one named check to prove the complete invariant
Divide the invariant into separately bound obligations
Add a new comprehensive linkage check
open_points.default_guess: Add a comprehensive linkage check and bind PLAT-REG-006 to it.

open_points.subject: PLAT-REG-001 Registry linkage check
open_points.text: “no service code generates a project id, the gateway only reads, and every project id the portal stores is one the Registry issued”
open_points.question: How must the bound check prove that every stored project_id is Registry-issued and that no code path can create one, including seeded or indirectly generated identifiers?
options: Inspect every project-id producer and every stored row without seed exclusions
Use a construction boundary that makes non-Registry project IDs unrepresentable
Narrow PLAT-REG-001 to the cases actually checked
open_points.default_guess: Test every storage producer and reject any stored ID not observed from the Registry boundary.

open_points.subject: PLAT-REG-005 witness bindings
open_points.text: “Witnesses, the focused Factory verification checks that assert it: PLAT-REG-005 [witness: verification:derived_views_uow_client_portal]; PLAT-REG-005 [witness: verification:api_transport_financial_policy_registry_gateway_client_portal].”
open_points.question: What bound check exercises every member of the closed RegistryFailureKind table and proves that none falls back to cached, client-supplied, or fabricated context?
options: Extend the named checks to cover the whole table and every forbidden fallback
Add one table-driven gateway check
Narrow PLAT-REG-005
open_points.default_guess: Add one table-driven gateway check covering every failure kind and fallback prohibition.

open_points.subject: INV-031 expense-recognition witness
open_points.text: “an unconfirmed, incomplete, unsupported-version or provider-carrying result is refused at decoding, by create_expense_from_recognition and over HTTP, with every table unchanged”
open_points.question: Must every named invalid form be exercised at all three stated boundaries, and if so which check demonstrates unsupported versions at decoding and HTTP plus incomplete/provider-carrying objects at the operation boundary?
options: Exercise every invalid form at every named boundary
State a smaller boundary matrix and bind tests to it
Split INV-031 into boundary-specific obligations
open_points.default_guess: Exercise every named invalid form at every boundary claimed by the Required tests item.

open_points.subject: INV-009 service-principal witness
open_points.text: “Witnesses, the focused Factory verification checks that assert it: INV-009 [witness: verification:service_identity_consumer_uow_client_portal].”
open_points.question: How does this binding establish viewer-grant uniqueness as well as service-principal-grant uniqueness?
options: Extend this check to both grant kinds
Bind it only to the service-principal half of a split invariant
Use one combined uniqueness check
open_points.default_guess: Split the invariant and bind this check only to the service-principal half.

open_points.subject: INV-009 viewer-grant witness
open_points.text: “Witnesses, the focused Factory verification checks that assert it: INV-009 [witness: verification:viewer_access_sqlite_uow_client_portal].”
open_points.question: How does this binding establish service-principal-grant uniqueness as well as viewer-grant uniqueness?
options: Extend this check to both grant kinds
Bind it only to the viewer half of a split invariant
Use one combined uniqueness check
open_points.default_guess: Split the invariant and bind this check only to the viewer half.

open_points.subject: INV-042 witness binding
open_points.text: “Witnesses, the focused Factory verification checks that assert it: INV-042 [witness: verification:project_tracking_audit_writer_sqlite_uow_client_portal].”
open_points.question: Which assertions demonstrate that WorkPayment never creates a factura or accounting posting and that payments_total is derived, in addition to replay behavior?
options: Extend the named check with forbidden-record and recomputation assertions
Split replay, non-accounting, and derivation into separately bound invariants
Narrow INV-042
open_points.default_guess: Split and bind each independently testable obligation.

open_points.subject: INV-043 witness binding
open_points.text: “Witnesses, the focused Factory verification checks that assert it: INV-043 [witness: verification:photo_management_uow_client_portal].”
open_points.question: Which assertions prove that every visibility-only change preserves all progress and financial data?
options: Compare all progress and financial tables and derived views before and after visibility changes
Split idempotency, ordering, and non-interference into separate invariants
Narrow INV-043
open_points.default_guess: Add complete before/after comparisons for progress and financial state.

open_points.subject: INV-037 money-policy witnesses
open_points.text: “Witnesses, the focused Factory verification checks that assert it: INV-037 [witness: verification:project_tracking_audit_writer_sqlite_uow_client_portal].” and “INV-037 [witness: verification:snapshot_import_sqlite_uow_client_portal].”
open_points.question: What bound check demonstrates the full invariant across all monetary boundaries: EUR-only input, explicit rejection without conversion, exact two-digit storage, and ROUND_HALF_UP derivation?
options: Create one comprehensive money-policy check
Split currency and decimal-rounding obligations into separately bound invariants
Extend both named checks until each independently proves INV-037

open_points.subject: INV-041 witness binding

open_points.question: Which assertions verify the exact weighted-progress formula, per-section rounding and summation, and unavailability when the denominator is zero?
options: Extend the named check with exact expected values and denominator-zero cases
Split completed-work and overall-progress formulas
Narrow INV-041
open_points.default_guess: Add exact formula cases, including missing progress and a zero denominator.

open_points.subject: INV-044 budget-derivation witness

options: Assert exact None in both budget and progress views
Bind a different check that already asserts exact None
Remove the claim from the Required tests item

Replace “enhanced audit” with the exact currently tested requirement
Bind a separate audit-provenance check

open_points.subject: INV-005 and INV-006 authorization-guard witness

Bind separate identity-module checks to individual cascade rows
Split the invariants by principal and revoked object

open_points.question: How does this binding establish disabled-account behavior and the service-principal half of INV-006, rather than only suspended staff behavior?

Bind it only to a split staff-status invariant
Use a combined principal-disablement check

Add a focused ordering check for authorize_snapshot_import

open_points.subject: changed re-publication outcome
open_points.text: A18 says “a changed re-publication is a conflict that changes nothing,” while R0-25 says every classified integrity conflict “is recorded as a fresh immutable import result with a fresh import_id and its snapshot.import audit.”
open_points.question: Does “changes nothing” mean no snapshot/budget/expense change while still appending the required import and audit records, or literally no table change?
options: Only snapshot, budget, plan and expense state remains unchanged; import and audit rows are appended
Every table remains unchanged
Integrity conflicts are no longer classified attempts
open_points.default_guess: Interpret it as no change to snapshot, budget, plan or expense state while still appending the import result and audit.

witness.initial: A snapshot already exists for project P, estimate E, version 1.
events: The producer republishes E version 1 with different content after passing access checks.
outcomes: Following A18 literally, the conflict changes no table.
Following R0-25 and M19–M20, the portal appends a fresh integrity-conflict SnapshotImportRecord and one snapshot.import audit while leaving the snapshot unchanged.
witness.observer: The producer reading the returned import_id and an administrator reading audit history.

open_points.subject: INV-026, INV-027 and INV-028 budget-derivation witness
open_points.text: “no table has a derived-value column,” “no service code deletes or replaces a portal section and no store surface removes one,” and “a changed re-publication is a conflict that changes nothing”
open_points.question: What non-heuristic assertions establish the absence of derived storage and section-removal paths, and what exact tables must remain unchanged on a conflicting re-publication?
options: Use explicit schema/API inventories and state the exempt import/audit rows
Keep heuristic scans as sufficient evidence
Narrow the invariants to the inspected names and surfaces
open_points.default_guess: Use explicit closed schema and store-surface inventories, and exempt the required append-only import/audit rows from conflict immutability.

open_points.subject: INV-032 and INV-036 intake witness

open_points.question: How does this binding establish atomic correction with allocation adjustment at every later commit point, when it exercises only intake scenarios?
options: Extend the check to correction and injected mid-operation failures
Bind it only to intake-specific obligations after splitting the invariant
Use the management check as the sole complete binding
open_points.default_guess: Split intake validity from correction atomicity and bind this check only to intake.

open_points.subject: INV-032 and INV-036 management witness
open_points.text: “Witnesses, the focused Factory verification checks that assert it: INV-032, INV-036 [witness: verification:expense_management_uow_client_portal].”
open_points.question: Which test injects failure between amount correction and allocation replacement and proves rollback leaves the old total and allocation set intact?
options: Add an injected-failure rollback test
Rely only on successful and pre-validation cases
Narrow atomicity to validation failures
open_points.default_guess: Add an injected-failure rollback test at the persistence boundary.

open_points.subject: INV-035 witness binding

open_points.question: Which assertion proves that an unconfirmed expense is excluded from financial totals, in addition to excluded confirmed expenses?
options: Seed an unconfirmed expense and assert it contributes nothing
Remove the confirmed-only clause
Bind a separate confirmed-only totals check
open_points.default_guess: Seed an unconfirmed expense and compare exact totals.

open_points.subject: INV-052 witness binding
open_points.text: “Witnesses, the focused Factory verification checks that assert it: INV-052 [witness: verification:snapshot_import_sqlite_uow_client_portal].”
open_points.question: Which tests attempt updates and deletions of both import records and audit records and prove they cannot commit?
options: Extend the named check with all four mutation attempts
Bind a generic append-only persistence check
Narrow INV-052
open_points.default_guess: Add direct update and deletion attempts for both record types.

open_points.subject: TXN-002 witness binding
open_points.text: “TXN-001, TXN-002: the transaction guard check [witness: verification:transaction_guard_client_portal].”
open_points.question: How must the check establish that the exact original domain-error object, including its contents, reaches the caller unchanged rather than merely an exception of the same type?
options: Assert object identity and unchanged fields
Define “unchanged” as same type only
Assert a complete serialized equality contract
open_points.default_guess: Assert object identity and unchanged contents.

open_points.subject: TRN-001 and TRN-003 runtime-behaviour witness
open_points.text: “TRN-001, TRN-002, TRN-003: the runtime behaviour check [witness: verification:runtime_behavior_client_portal].”
open_points.question: Which assertions prove rejected host/body requests never invoke a handler and that every credential, cookie and secret value is absent from actual emitted logs?
options: Instrument handler invocation and inject each secret class into real logging paths
Split the transport and logging invariants
Narrow the binding claim
open_points.default_guess: Instrument the handler and inspect actual logs after injecting representative values from every secret class.

open_points.subject: TRN-001 and TRN-003 transport-guard witness
open_points.text: “TRN-001, TRN-003: the transport guard check [witness: verification:transport_guard_client_portal].”
open_points.question: What check injects real credential and cookie values and inspects actual emitted log lines, rather than searching a synthetic non-secret record for selected words?
options: Extend the named check to real logging paths and secret values
Bind a dedicated log-redaction check
Narrow TRN-003
open_points.default_guess: Bind a dedicated log-redaction check using real emitted records.

open_points.subject: TRN-002 API-transport witness
open_points.text: “TRN-002: the API transport check [witness: verification:api_transport_financial_policy_registry_gateway_client_portal].”
open_points.question: Which assertion exercises viewer sign-out with a foreign Origin and proves it cannot succeed?
options: Add a foreign-origin sign-out request
Bind the runtime-behaviour check only if it fully covers this case
Split cookie-read and sign-out-origin obligations
open_points.default_guess: Add an explicit foreign-origin sign-out request and verify no session state changes.

open_points.subject: service-credential expires_at
open_points.text: The rules say a service credential’s `expires_at` is “kept as supplied, never replaced by the clock,” while the formal invariant says “an expiry it writes is that instant plus its TTL.”
open_points.question: When issuing a service credential with a caller-supplied expires_at that differs from now plus a configured TTL, must the portal preserve the supplied value or replace/validate it against a TTL-derived value?
options: Preserve every supplied service-credential expires_at exactly
Derive every persisted expiry from the operation instant plus TTL
Preserve supplied expiries, and restrict the TTL clause to portal-owned expiries
open_points.default_guess: Preserve supplied expiries and explicitly restrict the TTL clause to portal-owned expiries.

witness.initial: An active service principal exists; the operation clock instant is 2026-11-08T10:00:00 and the caller supplies expires_at 2026-12-01T00:00:00.
events: An administrator issues a service credential with that supplied expiry.
outcomes: The formal expiry rule stores the operation instant plus a TTL, or refuses the supplied value because it differs.
witness.observer: The administrator receiving the credential response and later authentication at the two possible expiry boundaries.

open_points.subject: one wall-clock reading and audit occurred_at
open_points.text: The source provides “one reading per request,” but “the occurred_at of an audit record appended through the audit writer” is an exception because “the writer takes it when it appends.”
open_points.question: For one audited request, does the audit writer take a second wall-clock reading, reuse the request’s single reading, or obtain an independently supplied audit instant without reading the host clock?
options: Audit append takes a second source reading despite the one-per-request rule
Audit occurred_at reuses the request reading
The operation supplies a separately obtained audit instant under a stated exception
open_points.default_guess: State an explicit exception allowing the audit writer a second source reading.

witness.initial: A staff mutation writes a business record and appends an AuditRecord in one HTTP request.
events: The operation reads the wall clock for its business timestamps.
Later in the same request, the audit writer appends the audit record.
outcomes: Under one reading per request, audit occurred_at equals the operation instant.
Under the audit-writer exception, the writer reads later and audit occurred_at may differ.
witness.observer: An administrator inspecting business and audit timestamps.

open_points.subject: clock invariant witness binding
open_points.text: “Witnesses, the focused Factory verification checks that assert it: one instant per operation [witness: verification:service_identity_consumer_uow_client_portal]; one instant per operation [witness: verification:staff_bootstrap_client_portal].”
open_points.question: What bindings cover every portal-owned multi-write timestamp, expiry equal to instant plus TTL, and preservation of every source-supplied time, rather than selected operations only?
options: Bind a test for every timestamp-writing operation as the preceding Required tests item requires
Split the invariant by operation and timestamp authority
Narrow the formal invariant to the two tested operations
open_points.default_guess: Bind one focused clock test for every timestamp-writing operation and explicit source-time preservation cases.

open_points.subject: configuration invariant witness bindings
open_points.text: “The existence of every timeout, TTL, rate limit and bound is invariant; its value is configuration.”
open_points.question: Which bound check enumerates every timeout, TTL, rate limit and bound and proves each exists and is configuration-driven?
options: Create a closed configuration inventory and test every member
Split the invariant into individually bound settings
Narrow the invariant to the currently tested viewer-entry and binary limits
open_points.default_guess: Create a closed inventory and a table-driven check for every member.

open_points.subject: security-review invariant witness
open_points.text: “Every category resolves to an accepted decision or an open question.”
open_points.question: How must the lint handle NOT_APPLICABLE categories so that each still resolves to an accepted decision or open question rather than only carrying an unbound rationale?
options: Require every NOT_APPLICABLE rationale to reference an accepted decision
Allow NOT_APPLICABLE as a third resolution and change the invariant
Remove NOT_APPLICABLE categories
open_points.default_guess: Require every NOT_APPLICABLE classification to reference the decision establishing non-applicability.
